"请在即将运行机器前添加洗涤剂：1. 只使用洗碗机专用粉末或块状洗涤剂，勿加入溶剂。2. 向右推动卡扣打开洗涤剂盒盖。<PIC> 3. 按程序表和脏污程度加入建议量，通常加至 15cm³ 或 25cm³ 刻度；若残渣已干涸，可同时加满 5cm³ 小格。<PIC> 4. 轻轻按下盒盖，听到“咔嗒”声即关紧。", ["Manual06_4", "Manual06_5"]
"在即将运行机器前添加洗涤块：先向右推动卡扣打开洗涤剂盒盖。<PIC> 按洗涤块包装说明，将建议量的洗涤块放入指定位置（如洗涤剂盒或碗篮等）。<PIC> 然后轻轻按下关闭洗涤剂盒盖，听到咔嗒声表示已关紧。使用多效洗涤块时，可选择程序后按半载/洗涤块键，直至洗涤块指示灯亮起，再启动并关闭机门。", ["Manual06_4", "Manual06_5"]

"亮碟剂可提高烘干效率，并防止餐具留下水渍或水垢。请仅使用洗碗机专用亮碟剂。查看亮碟剂指示灯（3）：常亮表示充足，熄灭则需添加。按下卡扣打开亮碟剂盒盖（B），加注至 MAX 刻度线后轻轻按下关闭盒盖，并擦净溢出的亮碟剂，避免产生泡沫、降低洗涤效果。<PIC> 将亮碟剂剂量旋钮手动调至 1–6 之间；若洗后有污渍调高，若手擦后有蓝色痕迹调低，出厂默认设置为 4。<PIC>", ["Manual06_5", "Manual06_7"]

"拆除前务必拔下电源插头。1 双手握住上盖向上拉起。<PIC> 2 握住背部滤网盖把手向前拉出。<PIC> 3 拆除滤网上的塑料包装。<PIC> 4 将滤网上下推入设备，确保贴合紧密。<PIC> 5 装回滤网盖：先插入底部固定卡槽，再向前滑动卡入顶部卡槽。<PIC> 6 双手握住上盖滑回原位，确保标识朝前。<PIC> 安装完成后，长按控制面板上的睡眠 + 自动键 5 秒以上初始化，红色滤网指示灯将熄灭。请将塑料包装远离儿童。", ["Manual03_0", "Manual03_1", "Manual03_2", "Manual03_3", "Manual03_4", "Manual03_5"]
"脚轮安装为可选：1. 在包装盒内找到小盒，内含 4 个脚轮和 8 颗螺丝。2. 用螺丝刀拆下空气净化器底部四个底座。3. 每个脚轮用两颗螺丝替换原底座。4. 保留拆下的底座和螺丝以备后续使用。若滤盒内无脚轮盒，请联系客服。", []

"空气净化器主要有以下模式：
1. 常规运行：按启动键开机，按上下键选择风速，可在 1 档（F1）至 18 档（F18）调节；特点是手动调节风速。<PIC>
2. 自动运行：开机后按自动键选择；每按一次可在自动运行和常规运行间切换。特点是根据室内空气质量自动调节风速，智能自动运行期间无法手动调风速。<PIC>
3. 涡轮风扇运行：开机并选择常规运行模式后，同时长按上下键 3 秒设置。特点是可更快净化室内空气。<PIC>
4. 睡眠运行：开机后按睡眠键选择，可用上下键调节 F1-F18 风速；再次按睡眠键恢复之前模式，关机后睡眠模式取消。特点是设备正常运行但显示屏熄灭，默认风速为 1 档，仅月亮图标亮起，避免干扰睡眠。<PIC>", ["Manual03_14", "Manual03_15", "Manual03_16", "Manual03_17"]
"室内空气质量（IAQ）指示灯用于实时查看室内空气质量，灯光环绕显示屏外缘。设备会根据传感器检测到的细颗粒物浓度，用四种颜色显示空气状态：蓝色好、绿色正常、黄色差、红色非常差。<PIC>", ["Manual03_20"]

"清洁前请务必拔下电源插头。1 双手握住设备上盖并向上拉起。<PIC> 2 握住背部滤网盖把手并向前拉出。<PIC> 3 拆下设备右侧灰尘传感器盖。<PIC> 4 用蘸少量水的棉签擦拭灰尘传感器镜头和进风口，再用干净干棉签彻底擦干。<PIC> 5 装回灰尘传感器盖、滤网盖，并将设备上盖标识朝前装回。注意：请勿使用丙酮、酒精等强腐蚀性化学试剂擦拭传感器部件。", ["Manual03_22", "Manual03_23", "Manual03_24", "Manual03_25"]

"控制台可提供运动重要信息，并可在运动时控制阻力等级；配有带触控按键的显示屏，用于浏览运动程序。主要按键包括阻力增/减、快速启动、程序、暂停/结束、目标追踪、确认、左右浏览及数值增/减等。<PIC> 显示方面，程序显示区展示运动曲线，列越高代表阻力越高，闪烁列为当前运动区间；还会显示强度、心率区间、目标、用户和成就信息。<PIC> 下部显示区可显示速度、时间、距离、当前阻力等级、转速、心率和卡路里等运动数据；心率数值为近似值，仅供参考。<PIC>", ["Manual14_21", "Manual14_22", "exercise_bikes_02"]

"编辑健身单车用户档案步骤：1. 在开机模式界面，按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮选择用户档案。2. 按确认按钮选择。3. 显示编辑提示和当前用户档案名称后，按确认开始编辑；如需退出，按暂停/结束按钮。4. 编辑姓名：用增加/减少浏览字母和空格，按左（◀）或右（▶）切换字符段，按确认接受用户名。5. 依次编辑年龄、体重、身高、性别，用增加/减少调节，每项完成后按确认。6. 在扫描提示中设置运动数据显示方式，按确认。7. 在编辑下部显示提示中自定义运动数据，用增加/减少和左/右按钮调整，完成后按确认。8. 控制台返回已选择用户的开机模式界面。", []
"可以。心率控制（HRC）程序会使用您的年龄和其他用户信息设置心率区间。设置时选择 HRC 等级后，可选择最大心率百分比：50–60%、60–70%、70–80% 或 80–90%；80–90% 区间运动前请咨询医生。燃脂建议目标为最大心率的 50–70%，并维持 20 分钟以上。基于年龄的通用目标心率请参考图表，个人最佳区间可能不同，建议咨询医生。<PIC>", ["Manual14_23"]
"体能测试程序用于评估体能水平提升：它会将功率输出（瓦特）与心率对比，体能提升后，相同心率下功率输出会增加。使用时控制台需能读取接触式心率传感器或心率监测仪信息；程序会选择初级/高级，并根据用户档案的年龄、体重计算体能得分。得分仅用于与自己的历史得分对比，不用于和其他用户比较。", []

"先在近岸练习，再到开阔水域；练习时不要启动发动机，并在水深至少齐胸处让艇漂浮。将熄火绳系在手腕上。登艇时游到艇尾，双手放在登艇平台上，单手抓住扶手 <PIC>；把身体拉到平台上呈跪姿，再移到座位上跨坐 <PIC>；将卡扣装到熄火开关，双手紧握车把，双脚放入脚坑 <PIC>。反复练习登艇与平衡，直到全过程能保持良好平衡。艇上配有登艇台阶，可放下辅助登艇，登艇后会自动复位 <PIC>。", ["Manual40_13", "Manual40_14", "Manual40_15", "Manual40_16"]
"滑航速度转弯时：保持油门配合车把，转向需要油门；先从平缓转向、低速开始，逐步提高速度并减小转弯半径，切勿急于求成 <PIC>；不要过度打车把，若艇体开始侧滑、转弯变钝，应将车把转回较小角度以恢复正常转向；可练习左右转向、圆圈和8字路线提升操控 <PIC>。", ["Manual40_26", "Manual40_27"]

"要保持操控性，应在半滑航速度下用油门配合车把转向；除拖曳速度外，转向时必须始终加油门，急转弯时要加大油门。松开油门后转向能力会迅速下降，重新加油门后艇体才恢复响应。<PIC> 大椭圆转弯：逐渐加速至半滑航速度，保持速度平稳，分别练习右转、左转，再完成完整椭圆。<PIC> 绕圈：保持速度不变，先右转绕大圈并逐渐缩小圈径，再练习左转。<PIC> 8字行驶：结合前述转弯与绕圈训练完成大8字路线，熟练后每次逐步缩小8字尺寸。<PIC>", ["Manual40_20", "Manual40_22", "Manual40_23", "Manual40_24"]
"中低速转弯时，应逐渐加速至半滑航速度，保持速度平稳再转向。摩托艇需通过油门与车把配合转向，除拖曳速度外，转向时必须始终加油门；急转弯时，转向同时必须加大油门。若松开油门，转向能力会迅速下降，发动机减速后艇体不再响应车把，需逐渐重新加油门恢复操控。绕圈练习时应保持速度不变，并逐渐缩小圈径。<PIC>", ["Manual40_20"]
"拖曳速度是最低操控速度，几乎不加油门。操作时先登艇并观察周围人员、物体及其他船只；启动发动机后先直线行驶；随后开始转向，按长约15–21米（50–70英尺）的大8字路线行驶，且不加油门，以练习平顺转向。<PIC> 还可将车把向任意方向转到最大，让艇做360°转向，并分别练习顺时针与逆时针转向，熟悉艇体对车把动作的响应。", ["Manual40_19"]

"松开油门手柄，让摩托艇靠水阻减速滑行直至停止；摩托艇没有独立制动系统，全速松油或停机后约需90米才完全停止，距离会受载重、水面状况和风向影响。<PIC> 松油后转向能力会下降，若判断停不住或前方有障碍，应观察四周，重新加油门并转向避让；降至拖曳速度后再转向。<PIC> EX Deluxe可握紧RiDE手柄辅助减速，停车距离约缩短30%，但RiDE不是规避危险的制动装置。", ["Manual40_21", "Manual40_25"]

"避免碰撞应做到：持续观察周围人员、物体及其他船只，留意影响视线或遮挡视野的环境；以安全速度谨慎驾驶，并保持安全距离；不要紧跟其他摩托艇或船只，不要靠近他人喷水或溅水；避开水下障碍物和浅水区；尽早采取避让行动。记住，摩托艇和其他船只没有刹车装置，转向避开物体时不要松开油门手柄，因为转向需要油门动力。启动前务必检查油门与转向操控是否正常，并遵守航行规则和当地法规。<PIC>", ["Manual40_0"]
"发动机停机步骤：1. 将油门手柄完全向左推。<PIC> 2. 将发动机开关置于“OFF”位置。<PIC> 3. 将燃油开关手柄置于“OFF”位置。<PIC>", ["Manual31_16", "Manual31_17", "Manual31_18"]
"手册部件说明中列出的主要部件包括：油箱、油箱盖、燃油开关、空气滤清器盖、火花塞、消音器、阻风门手柄、发动机开关、机油加注口盖、放油螺塞、反冲启动器、机油警告灯、油门手柄、注水螺塞、放水螺塞。<PIC><PIC>", ["pump_16", "pump_17"]
"清洗油箱滤网步骤：1. 拆下油箱盖及油箱滤网（①油箱盖，②油箱滤网）。2. 用溶剂清洗滤网，如有损坏则更换。3. 擦干滤网后装回。4. 务必拧紧油箱盖。<PIC>", ["Manual31_32"]
"排放燃油时应远离吸烟或明火。步骤：1. 排空油箱、燃油开关及化油器浮子室（③为化油器放油螺塞）。2. 向油箱内倒入一杯 SAE 10W30 或 20W40 发动机机油。3. 晃动油箱，使内壁均匀附着机油。4. 排出多余机油。<PIC>", ["Manual31_41"]

"按以下顺序诊断并处理：1. 启动前确认泵体内已注满水至上限，否则可能损坏机械密封。<PIC> 2. 检查注水螺塞、放水螺塞是否松动，松动则拧紧。3. 检查软管接头或卡箍是否松动，软管必须安装牢固，否则会进气导致无法抽水；松动则拧紧。<PIC> 4. 检查 O 形圈或垫片是否损坏，损坏则更换。5. 若机械密封损坏，应咨询经销商。另：水泵应放在稳固平面并尽量靠近水源，吸程越高，注水时间越长，出水量越小。", ["Manual31_10", "Manual31_4"]

"设置日期：按菜单键进入设备菜单，显示 PROG 后按 + 或 - 选择“日期”，按选择键；年份闪烁时按 + 或 - 调整年份并按选择键，再调整月份并按选择键，最后调整日期并按选择键保存退出。\n设置时间：按菜单键进入设备菜单，显示 PROG 后按 + 或 - 选择“时间”，按选择键；按 + 或 - 选择 12 小时制或 24 小时制并按选择键；再按 + 或 - 调整小时、分钟，每步按选择键，最后按选择键保存并退出。", []

"系统运行设置：按“模式”键循环切换，直到显示所需模式并保持激活。可选模式因型号及系统设置而异：自动=按需自动选择供暖或制冷；供暖=仅控制供暖；制冷=仅控制制冷；应急供暖=仅适用于带辅助加热的热泵；关闭=供暖和制冷关闭，但风扇在开启/循环模式下仍可运行。<PIC>\n风扇运行设置：按“风扇”键循环切换，直到显示所需模式并保持激活。可选模式因系统设置而异：自动=仅在供暖或制冷运行时启动；开启=持续运行；循环=随机运行约33%的时间。<PIC>\n注：由于压缩机保护，供暖/制冷指示灯可能闪烁5分钟。", ["Manual36_29", "Manual36_30"]

"每天可设置4个时段，工作日和周末可设置不同参数：起床、离家、回家、睡眠；离家和睡眠通常设为节能温度，建议使用预设设置以降低供暖/制冷能耗。<PIC> 调整步骤：按菜单键<PIC>；显示 PROG 后按选择键，显示“开启”后再按选择键；用 + 或 - 选择要编辑的日期/日期组并按选择键；选择要编辑的时段（起床、离家、回家、睡眠）并按选择键；保持该时段开启，或按 + 后按选择键关闭；用 + 或 - 调整开始时间、供暖设定温度和制冷设定温度，并按选择键确认；对其他时段重复操作；完成后按主页键保存并返回主界面。<PIC><PIC>", ["Manual36_31", "thermostat_04", "thermostat_05", "thermostat_06"]
"按温控器上的 + 或 - 将温度调整到所需设定值即可，无需其他操作。该临时设定会保持到下一个预定时间段开始，不会更改已编程日程。若要取消临时保持，按 + 或 -，然后按取消键。<PIC>", ["Manual36_32"]
"主界面出现警报图标时，进入菜单查看警报以获取错误/警报代码；查看后警报符号会保留至清除。出现警报图标时，对照警报代码表确定问题。暂态警报可取消，取消后将在7天后再次显示；也可清除警报。", []

"热泵接线时，将每根标记电线与新温控器上相同字母匹配并插入对应端子；若插入困难，可按下端子旁按钮。<PIC> 若标签不匹配，按备用接线处理：R滑动开关保持向上（1根线）；若旧温控器同时有V和VR线，停止并联系专业安装人员；若有单独O和B线，将B线接至C端子，若C端子已接线则停止并联系专业安装人员；若有Y1、W1和W2线，停止并联系专业安装人员。<PIC>", ["Manual36_35", "Manual36_36"]
"安全更换电池：出现低电量图标时应立即更换；即使未出现，也应每年更换一次，或离家超过一个月前更换。更换时建议使用碱性电池，在温控器背面装入两节AA碱性电池 <PIC>。若在两分钟内完成更换，无需重新设置时间和日期；其他设置会永久存储，无需电池供电。", ["Manual36_22"]

"标签与端子不匹配时，不要按颜色猜接线；请按系统类型使用备用接线图：常规系统按图连接 <PIC>，热泵系统按图连接 <PIC>。常规系统：若同时接 R 和 Rc，或旧温控器同时有 R 和 RH，将 R 滑动开关拨至向下（2 根线）；R 接 Rc，RH 接 R；仅 1 根 C/C1 接 C，若有 2 根 C/C1 则分别用电工胶带包裹且不连接。热泵系统：R 滑动开关保持向上（1 根线）；若同时有 V 和 VR，或有 Y1、W1、W2，停止并联系专业安装人员。", ["Manual36_34", "Manual36_36"]

"可尝试以下故障排除方法：1. 屏幕空白：若使用电池供电，确认已正确安装全新 AA 碱性电池。2. 无法切换至制冷模式：检查系统设置 220，确保设为 1 或 2。3. 需要供暖时风扇不启动：检查系统设置 205，确保与供暖设备匹配。4. 制冷模式下供暖系统运行：检查系统设置 200 或 218，确保与供暖和制冷设备匹配。5. 供暖或制冷系统无响应：将系统设为供暖并确保设定温度高于室内温度；制冷时确保设定温度低于室内温度；检查断路器并在必要时复位，确认供暖/制冷系统电源开关已打开、炉门紧闭，并等待 5 分钟。6. 屏幕上“供暖开启/制冷开启”闪烁：压缩机保护功能已启动，等待 5 分钟让系统安全重启。7. 热泵供暖吹冷风或制冷吹热风：检查系统设置 200 或 218，确保与设备匹配。", []
"处理器单元的关键组件包括：正面有状态指示灯（白色：已开机；红色：待机模式）、AUX端口、HDMI输出端口 <PIC>；背面有HDMI电视端口、HDMI PS4端口、USB端口、DC IN 12V接口和通风口 <PIC>。", ["Manual38_1", "Manual38_2"]
"手册中的耳机为立体声耳机，耳塞出厂已安装M号，可更换为S号或L号以获得更贴合的佩戴效果。<PIC> 更换时，旋转耳塞后将其拔下；装回时请牢固安装，防止使用中意外脱落。<PIC>", ["Manual38_3", "Manual38_4"]
"清洁前请拔下电源线并断开所有线缆。将遮光罩从VR头显上取下，用水清洗；再用软布完全擦干后装回头显。重新安装时，将遮光罩上的凸点与头显上的13个孔对齐。请勿使用溶剂、其他化学药剂或经化学处理的清洁布。<PIC>", ["Manual38_5"]
"游玩区域的推荐尺寸约为宽 3.0 m、深 1.9 m；使用前请检查并清理大于游玩区域的活动空间。<PIC>", ["Manual38_0"]

"使用和操作VR头显时应注意：
1. 使用前阅读并遵守说明书及配套硬件手册；VR头显不适用于12岁以下儿童。
2. 疲劳、头晕、恶心、醉酒、服药、平衡感受损或患有严重疾病时不要使用；有癫痫或癫痫史者使用前咨询医生。
3. 使用前清理大于游玩区域的活动空间，远离墙壁、楼梯、家具等障碍物，并防止宠物、他人或障碍物进入。
4. 佩戴时待在游玩区域中央，尽量坐姿，避免剧烈或过度动作；站立使用时严格遵循应用指示。
5. 开始前及使用中检查线缆是否缠绕身体或四肢。
6. 出现头晕、视觉异常、恶心、方向障碍、疼痛、癫痫发作等不适时立即停止使用，必要时就医，症状消失前不要从事需要良好视力、平衡感或协调能力的活动。
7. 初次使用建议短时间体验；不要在震动或不稳定环境中使用。
8. 连接前检查接口无灰尘和细小杂物；不要损坏电源线和电源适配器，不要抓着线缆甩动设备。
9. 待头显追踪灯熄灭后再取下VR头显或拔下连接线；灯亮时取下或拔线可能导致设备故障。
10. 不要在产品上放置物品、投掷、摔落或使其受到强烈撞击；雷雨时不要触碰电源线、电源适配器或处理器单元。
11. 防止液体或细小颗粒进入接口、通风口等；不要暴露在灰尘、烟雾或蒸汽中。
12. 产品开机时避免长时间接触处理器单元、电源适配器或通风口热风，以免低温烫伤。
13. 将设备放在幼儿接触不到的地方，避免吞咽零件、拉扯线缆、缠绕线缆或造成设备坠落。
14. 正确佩戴VR头显，不要将调节旋钮拧得过紧，不要过度推入或拉出镜罩，并定期检查佩戴状态。
15. 保持附着传感器无遮挡，避免屏幕长时间显示同一画面导致永久残影。
16. 使用耳机时保持安全音量；出现耳鸣、耳部不适或听觉模糊时停止使用并检查听力。
17. 不要使用溶剂或其他化学药剂清洁产品，避免橡胶或乙烯基材料长时间接触产品；不要拆卸或改装本产品及配件。
18. 若从寒冷环境移至温暖环境出现结露，应关闭产品、断开电源，待水分完全蒸发后再使用。
19. 若出现高温提示，应关闭系统并静置，待处理器单元冷却后移至通风良好位置再继续使用。", []

"保修政策通常包含：保修期限、保障对象、保修范围、维修或更换方式、技术支持与保修申请流程、适用法律及消费者额外法定权利。享受保修需提供购买凭证，且仅覆盖原始消费者购买的产品；若保修期内经合理判定为故障，可视库存提供维修或更换，更换品可为全新或翻新、功能相近且价值相等或更高的产品。\n不包含：未经许可改装产品或序列号/保修标签；非制造缺陷损坏；意外、滥用、误用、疏忽、火灾、进水、雷击、自然灾害、未按说明操作等造成的损坏、老化或故障；安装不当、未经授权更改/改装或非授权维修；运输途中损坏；正常磨损；以及间接或继发性损害。", []
"保修项下的责任仅限于自行选择维修或更换故障产品；不对任何间接或继发性损害负责，包括服务中断、数据丢失、业务损失，或因产品及其使用、持有相关的民事侵权责任。手册还说明不保证产品满足所有需求，用户需自行判断适用性；除规定外不存在其他明示或默示担保。", []
"设置功能键盘：1. 将 USB-C 线连接键盘背面接口，另一端连接电脑可用的 USB 2.0 或更高速度接口。2. 将腕托（仅全尺寸及无小键盘版本）安装到键盘正面，腕托为磁吸设计，会自动吸附并居中。3. 如需更高打字倾斜角度，可展开键盘底部两层可调节支撑脚，选择中高两档角度。", []
"拆卸：使用附赠拔轴器从顶部夹住轴体，工具两端沿轴体前后方向放置，按下轴体固定在定位板上的两个卡扣后取出；不要刮擦上盖面板，也无需从轴体下方撬动，仅夹住轴体外壳底部两侧即可。<PIC> 安装：安装前确认所有针脚笔直，两个金属针脚与键盘轴座插孔对应后，垂直向下用力插入键盘插槽；正确插入后，轴体外壳两侧应紧贴键盘上盖面板。<PIC>", ["Manual21_14", "Manual21_15"]

"使用方法：1. 前往官网下载并安装最新版 CAM 软件。2. 在 CAM 中设置键盘配置文件并保存至键盘；键盘自带 4 个板载配置文件，保存后无需运行 CAM 也可使用已存储的灯光、宏命令等功能。3. 按 FN+F1/F2/F3/F4 可切换对应 1 至 4 号配置文件。4. 可在 CAM 的键盘/灯光设置中逐键自定义 RGB 灯光，在键盘/宏命令设置中创建宏命令，在键盘/按键重映射设置中创建自定义按键绑定，并按需保存至配置文件。", []
"在硬件模式下：按 FN+F1/F2/F3/F4 可切换至配置文件 1–4；配置文件 1–4 自带四种默认 RGB 灯光模式。若已将自定义灯光分配至某板载配置文件，切换到该配置文件时会激活自定义灯光。", []
"安装挡泥板：先将挡泥板侧转，然后向上滑入左侧把手管，注意不要让“凸点”卡入1号孔。<PIC> 接着调整挡泥板，使“凸点”卡入2号孔。<PIC>", ["rideon_motorcycle_01", "rideon_motorcycle_02"]
"安装前轮：将前轴穿过两侧把手管和前轮，并在两侧把手管内外都装上垫片；再用两个螺母将前轴和车轮固定到把手管上，用随附扳手拧紧螺母直至螺纹尽头。<PIC> 组装后检查车轮与把手管间隙：若间隙过大、车轮不稳，可在车轮与把手管之间加装额外垫片；若车轮卡死，则减少一片垫片，确保车轮能自由转动。<PIC>", ["Manual26_6", "Manual26_7"]
"鼠标需使用两节 AA 电池：1. 按下按钮，电池仓盖弹出。<PIC> 2. 按照鼠标内部标注的正负极（+ 和 -）装入两节 AA 电池。<PIC> 3. 装回电池仓盖。<PIC>", ["Manual27_1", "Manual27_2", "Manual27_3"]

"安装前，请先将 USB 蓝牙接收器插入电脑 USB 接口。步骤如下：1. 将附带安装光盘放入光驱。2. 驱动程序会自动加载；若未自动加载，请双击光驱中 bin 文件夹内的 Setup.exe。3. 欢迎界面点击“下一步”。<PIC> 4. 阅读协议，选择“我接受许可协议中的条款”，点击“下一步”。<PIC> 5. 确认安装文件夹；如需更改路径点击“更改”，然后点击“下一步”。<PIC> 6. 点击“安装”开始安装，等待完成。<PIC> 7. 出现完成界面表示安装完成。<PIC> 8. 拔下接收器并重新插入，鼠标将自动配对；点击“完成”退出安装。系统提示重启时，点击“是”立即重启或“否”稍后重启。<PIC>", ["Manual27_4", "Manual27_5", "Manual27_6", "Manual27_7", "Manual27_8", "Manual27_9"]
"卸载 WIDCOMM 蓝牙驱动程序步骤：1. 拔下 USB 蓝牙接收器。2. 点击“开始 > 设置 > 控制面板 > 添加或删除程序”。3. 在程序列表中选择 WIDCOMM 蓝牙软件，点击“删除”。4. 等待系统卸载完成。5. 卸载完成后按提示重启电脑，可点击“是”立即重启，或“否”稍后重启。", []
"Windows 快速配对步骤：1. 将 USB 蓝牙接收器插入电脑 USB 接口。2. 按下鼠标底部的配对按钮。<PIC> 3. 按下 USB 蓝牙接收器底部按钮，直到 LED 指示灯每秒闪烁一次，表示接收器开始搜索待配对设备。<PIC> 4. 移动鼠标确认连接成功。（本款鼠标不含接收器销售。）", ["Manual27_10", "Manual27_11"]
"先按说明安装 WIDCOMM 蓝牙驱动程序。然后按下 USB 蓝牙接收器按钮，直到出现人机接口设备（HID）界面 <PIC>。鼠标连接成功后会出现确认信息，点击确认连接正确的鼠标 <PIC>。", ["Manual27_12", "Manual27_13"]
"可通过鼠标电量 LED 指示灯查看：电量耗尽时 LED 会变为琥珀色，需立即更换电池；顶部 LED 与底部指示灯状态一致。<PIC> 如需查看更详细电量信息，请进入“控制面板 > 鼠标 > 蓝牙”。<PIC>", ["Manual27_14", "Manual27_15"]
"首次使用蓝牙驱动程序：双击系统托盘中的蓝牙图标 <PIC>；蓝牙初始配置向导启动后，按屏幕说明完成配置。配置完成后会出现 HID 界面并开始搜索蓝牙设备 <PIC>；点击要连接的 HID 设备，并按屏幕说明启用所选设备。", ["Manual27_16", "Manual27_17"]
"连接其他 HID 设备：1. 确保 USB 蓝牙接收器已插入电脑。2. 将要连接的蓝牙设备设置为可被蓝牙驱动程序搜索。3. 按下 USB 蓝牙接收器按钮，直至出现 HID 界面。4. 从下拉菜单中选择要搜索的设备类型。<PIC> 5. 显示检测到的设备后，点击该设备，驱动程序将引导您启用连接。", ["Manual27_18"]
"拆卸烤箱门前，请佩戴防护手套，确保烤箱已冷却，并断开电源。步骤：1. 完全打开烤箱门。2. 抬起卡扣并向前推至极限位置。<PIC> 3. 将烤箱门关至最大角度（A），向上抬起（B）并转动（C），直至脱开（D）。<PIC>", ["oven_01", "oven_02"]
"安装烤箱门前，请佩戴防护手套，确保烤箱已冷却，并断开电源。步骤：1. 将铰链装入对应位置。2. 完全打开烤箱门。3. 放下两个卡扣。4. 关闭烤箱门。", []
"操作前佩戴防护手套，确保烤箱已冷却，并断开电源。1. 取下侧边配件支架格栅。<PIC> 2. 轻轻拉出顶部加热元件。<PIC> 3. 将其向下放下。<PIC> 复位时，抬起加热元件并轻轻向自身方向拉动，确保其支撑在侧支架上。", ["oven_03", "oven_04", "oven_05"]
"更换后部灯（如有）：1. 断开烤箱电源。2. 拧下灯罩 <PIC>，更换灯泡后再拧回灯罩 <PIC>。3. 重新接通烤箱电源。注意：仅使用25‑40W/230V E‑14、耐温300℃白炽灯；灯罩复位前请勿使用烤箱。", ["oven_06", "oven_07"]
"接油盘（图1）可放在烤架下方，用于收集油脂和食物碎屑；也可作为烤盘烹饪肉类、鸡肉、鱼类等，可搭配蔬菜使用。使用时向接油盘中倒入少量水，可避免油脂飞溅及冒烟。烧烤肉类时，建议在烤架正下方放置加有半升水的接油盘收集肉汁，并按需补充水分。<PIC>", ["oven_08"]
"清洁烤箱外部前，请待烤箱冷却并断开电源，不要使用蒸汽清洁设备。请勿使用腐蚀性或研磨性清洁剂；若意外接触设备，请立即用湿布擦拭。外部表面用湿布清洁，污渍严重时可在水中加入几滴洗洁精，最后用干布擦干。", []
"烤架用于烧烤食物，也可作为锅具、蛋糕模及其他烹饪容器的支架；可放在任意可用层位，凸面朝上或朝下均可。烧烤肉类时，厚肉块可降低烤架位置，烹饪至三分之二时间时翻面；建议在烤架正下方放置加有半升水的接油盘收集肉汁。<PIC>", ["oven_10"]
"催化侧面板带有特殊微孔搪瓷涂层，可吸附油脂飞溅物；烹饪油脂较多的食物后，建议执行自动清洁程序。", []
"烤盘用于烘焙饼干、蛋糕及披萨。做披萨时，可在烤盘上轻微刷油，以保证披萨底部酥脆；烹饪至三分之二时间时再撒马苏里拉芝士。<PIC>", ["oven_09"]
"烤架烤盘套装包含烤架（6a）和搪瓷容器（6b）。使用时，将该套装放置在烤架（3）上，并配合烧烤功能使用。<PIC>", ["oven_13"]
"油脂过滤器仅用于油脂较多的烹饪。使用时将其挂在烤箱腔体后壁、风扇对面位置；可配合热风循环功能使用，且可放入洗碗机清洗。", []
"滑动搁架可在烹饪过程中将烤架与接油盘半拉出使用；适用于所有配件，并可放入洗碗机清洗。<PIC>", ["oven_15"]

"肩带为另售品。安装方法：1. 用卡扣安装工具打开肩带卡扣。<PIC> 2. 将挂绳环钩入卡扣开口，用另一只手按住卡扣并取出工具。<PIC> 3. 将卡扣完全旋转穿过每个挂绳环，直到咔哒闭合。<PIC> 4. 将肩带穿过每个卡扣。<PIC> 注意：肩带仅作肩带使用，请勿套在脖子上；不要遮挡相纸出口。", ["Manual29_12", "hybrid_instant_camera_03", "hybrid_instant_camera_04", "hybrid_instant_camera_05"]
"装入电池：1. 滑动电池盖将其打开。<PIC> 2. 按照电池上的箭头指示装入电池，确保电池上的黄线与相机上的标记对齐。<PIC> 3. 关闭电池盖。<PIC>", ["Manual29_13", "Manual29_14", "Manual29_15"]

"装入前请注意：相纸用完前请勿打开后盖；仅使用 instax SQUARE 拍立得相纸；装入时切勿按压相纸盒背面的两个矩形孔。装入步骤：1. 按住相仓锁按钮，然后将拨杆向右滑动，直至相仓略微打开。<PIC> 2. 握住相纸盒两侧，将相纸盒底部对准相仓凹槽，然后平直插入。<PIC> 3. 关闭后盖，并确保后盖锁咔哒到位。<PIC> 4. 关闭后盖时黑色相纸保护盖会自动弹出，请从相纸出口取出。<PIC>", ["Manual29_26", "Manual29_27", "hybrid_instant_camera_01", "hybrid_instant_camera_02"]
"确认相纸用完后（拍摄画面右侧所有点呈灰色），按住相仓锁按钮（1），将拨杆向右滑动，直到相仓略微打开 <PIC>。然后握住相纸盒上的矩形孔，平直拉出相纸盒 <PIC>。", ["Manual29_28", "Manual29_29"]
"将相机侧面的打印模式选择器切换到“AUTO”即可设置自动打印模式。拍摄画面会出现自动打印图标，图像保存后会立即开始打印。<PIC><PIC><PIC>", ["Manual29_30", "Manual29_31", "Manual29_32"]
"将相机侧面的打印模式选择器切换到“MANUAL”即可（手动打印模式为默认设置）。<PIC> 设置后，拍摄画面会出现手动打印图标；图像会保存到内存中，可稍后选择并打印，而不是立即打印。<PIC>", ["Manual29_33", "Manual29_34"]
"顺时针转动镜头环（电源开关）开机。<PIC> 手持相机并确认构图。<PIC> 可选择拍摄模式或图像效果；半按快门对焦：成功时相机会发出蜂鸣声并显示绿色对焦框，失败时显示红色对焦框。然后完全按下快门拍摄，照片会保存到相机内存；若打印模式为自动打印，图像将被打印。拍摄时请双手持机，注意不要遮挡闪光灯、镜头或相纸出口。", ["Manual29_36", "Manual29_37"]
"Before first use: 1) Remove all packing material. 2) Remove any stickers or labels, if available, from the appliance. 3) Thoroughly clean the appliance as indicated in the cleaning chapter.", []

"Open the engine hood, then look for the emission control information label. The approval labels are attached to each engine unit and to the inside of the engine compartment, marked as “1” in the illustrations. <PIC> <PIC>", ["Manual09_6", "Manual09_7"]

"The provided manual excerpts do not describe a “battery conversion feature” or give steps for using it before sailing. They only state that the batteries and switch assembly are in the battery compartment, and that the boat has two batteries: a start battery for the starter motor and a house battery for accessory circuits such as lighting, bilge pump, blowers, and audio system. The battery compartment is on the port side at the stern; unhook the latch and open the lid to access it. <PIC> <PIC>", ["Manual09_157", "Manual09_158"]

"The boat is steered by turning the steering wheel in the direction you want to travel. <PIC> Turning the wheel changes the angle of the jet thrust nozzles at the rear, which changes the boat’s direction; the articulating keel moves with the nozzles. <PIC> Jet thrust also affects steering: more throttle produces more thrust and a sharper turn, so the throttle must be above idle when turning except at trolling speed. Because the boat steers from the stern, the stern swings opposite the direction of the turn. <PIC>", ["Manual09_52", "Manual09_53", "Manual09_239"]

"If “Over Temperature” appears and the buzzer sounds, immediately reduce engine speed, return to shore or maneuver to a safe location, and check for water discharge from the cooling water pilot outlets. If water is not flowing, do not continue to run the engines. Check whether the intake grates are clogged. <PIC> If the cause cannot be found/corrected: for single-engine overheating, shut off that engine and return using the other engine at no-wake speed; for both engines overheating, get towed if possible, or operate both engines just slightly above idle while returning to shore.", ["Manual09_96"]

"On your phone, turn Bluetooth ON and connect to the available device “earphones”. <PIC> To activate the music app, press and hold until the first beep, then let go; playback resumes where you left off. If nothing plays, tap again. <PIC>", ["Manual12_6", "earphones_01"]

"Use the wet storage compartment located under the swim platform. To open it, pull the lock handle up, turn it clockwise, and open the rear platform hatch. <PIC> Store wet items in the wet storage compartment. <PIC> To close it, close the rear platform hatch, turn the lock handle counterclockwise and make sure the hatch is securely closed, then push the lock handle down. Make sure storage compartments are securely closed before getting underway; the engines will not start if the rear platform hatch is not securely closed.", ["Manual09_143", "Manual09_144"]
"The battery compartment is located on the port side of the boat at the stern. To open it, unhook the latch, then open the battery compartment lid. <PIC> <PIC>", ["Manual09_157", "Manual09_158"]

"The manual does not provide instructions for installing the anchor light while the boat is moving. For 210FSH SPORT, pull the lock tab, raise the anchor light, then return the lock tab to its original position to lock it in place. <PIC> For 210FSH DELUXE, the excerpt only states to install the removable anchor light before using/checking the navigation and anchor lights switch. Then push the upper side of the switch and check that the bow light and anchor light come on. <PIC>", ["Manual09_160", "Manual09_223"]

"Before use, make sure the shut-off valve is open. The jet wash must be used only by a passenger who is not operating the boat; the operator must attach the engine shut-off cord to their PFD and keep scanning for people, objects, and other watercraft. To use it: 1) Connect the coil hose to the hose fitting. <PIC> 2) Start the engines. 3) Push the jet wash switch. <PIC> Water starts after about 5 seconds; push the switch again to adjust the water flow among 3 levels. 4) Move the jet wash handle lever to discharge water. <PIC> To stop: push the jet wash switch, stop the engines, then push the collar on the hose fitting inward and disconnect the coil hose. <PIC> If water leaks or any problem occurs, close the shut-off valve immediately.", ["Manual09_173", "Manual09_174", "Manual09_177", "Manual09_178"]

"To turn the water supply on or off: stop the engines, open the rear platform hatch, remove the inspection cover <PIC>, then turn the shut-off valve 90° clockwise to turn the water supply on, or 90° counterclockwise to turn it off <PIC>. Reinstall the inspection cover and close the rear platform hatch.", ["Manual09_179", "Manual09_180"]

"To remove the bimini top:
1. Open the flap on the starboard side of the bimini top. <PIC>
2. Loosen the ratchet, then loosen the strap securing the bimini top. <PIC>
3. Slowly pull the bimini top toward the bow and remove it.

To remove the bimini top from the boat: first store it in the fully collapsed position, then remove the main pole mounting pins from the main pole mounting brackets, and remove the bimini top from the boat. <PIC>", ["Manual09_183", "Manual09_184", "Manual09_193"]

"For the 210FSH SPORT, the bimini top can be used as a sunshade or rain cover. To install it, simply reverse the removal steps: open the starboard-side flap, route/secure the bimini top, tighten the strap with the ratchet, and close the flap. <PIC> <PIC> <PIC>\nFor the 210FSH DELUXE, install the bimini top by reversing the removal steps, then make sure the main pole mounting pins are securely installed. <PIC>", ["Manual09_182", "Manual09_183", "Manual09_184", "Manual09_193"]

"To store the bimini top in the upright position: 1) Remove the lock pins, then push the center poles down. <PIC> 2) Pull the bimini top toward the bow. <PIC> 3) Install the storage cover. Notice: Do not exceed 72 km/h (45 mph) with the bimini top in the up position, and do not trailer the boat with the bimini top in the upright storage position.", ["Manual09_189", "Manual09_190"]

"If “Low Oil Pressure” appears while underway, reduce engine speed, return to shore or maneuver to a safe location, then check the engine oil level. When checking on water, moor the boat so it will not drift. With the engine stopped, launch/keep the boat level, look in all directions, start the engine, idle for 6 minutes or more; idle an additional 5 minutes if ambient temperature is 20°C (68°F) or less, then stop the engine and check the oil level. If low, add enough engine oil to reach the proper level. If the oil level is sufficient, have a Boat Dealer check the engine.", []

"Turn on the bilge pump switch to operate the bilge pump. <PIC> Water in the bilge is drained through the bilge pump outlet. <PIC> Even if the switch is not turned on, the pump will automatically detect excessive bilge water and drain most of it, even when the battery switches are off. The bilge pump indicator light comes on while the pump is operating. <PIC>", ["Manual09_201", "Manual09_202", "Manual09_203"]

"Perform the navigation/anchor lights switch check as follows: for 210FSH DELUXE, install the anchor light first. Locate the navigation and anchor lights switch <PIC>. Push the upper side of the switch and check that the bow light <PIC> and anchor light come on: DELUXE <PIC>, SPORT <PIC>. Push the lower side and check that only the anchor light comes on. Put the switch in the middle position and check that the bow light and anchor light are off. For 210FSH DELUXE, remove the anchor light after the check.", ["Manual09_223", "Manual09_224", "Manual09_225", "Manual09_226"]

"To start the engines: make sure the engine shut-off switch clip is attached, put the remote control levers in neutral, then turn the main switch keys to START and release them when the engines start; the keys return automatically to ON. If the engines do not start after 5 seconds of cranking, release the keys and wait at least 15 seconds before trying again. <PIC>", ["Manual09_237"]

"Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the boat to travel, right or left. Keep the throttle open above idle when turning, except at trolling speed; steering depends on both steering wheel position and throttle. Do not pull the remote control levers back to idle to steer away from objects—you need throttle to steer. At trolling speed, the boat can turn gradually with steering wheel position alone. Remember the stern swings opposite your turn, so ensure passengers are holding on before turning.", []

"To cross wakes or swells, adjust your speed and choose the crossing angle. Usually, a slower speed and quartering the wake—crossing at an angle—will reduce the jolt. When quartering, the boat may try to steer away from the wake or swell; this may be less noticeable at about 45° but can be strong at smaller angles such as 10°, so be prepared to steer and balance as needed. <PIC> Crossing groups of wakes or swells is harder than crossing one. Small swells are easier than larger swells or wakes, and sharp wakes give more jolt than broad swells. <PIC>", ["Manual09_249", "Manual09_250"]

"To load the boat onto the trailer: (1) Disconnect the trailer lights from the towing vehicle. (2) Back the trailer down the ramp as close to 90° to the shoreline as possible. If possible, have a second person stand to the side of the trailer as an observer. Stop when the tops of the trailer’s fenders are about 3 inches above the waterline.", []

"Proper flushing is not possible with the boat in the water. After putting the boat on the trailer, flush the cooling system to prevent clogging from salt, sand, or dirt. Connect the garden hose adapter to a garden hose <PIC>. Then loosen and remove the flush hose connector cap, and insert the garden hose adapter into the flush hose connector by pushing and twisting it until securely connected.", ["Manual09_257"]

"WARNING: Do not use fuses with a higher amperage than recommended; an improper rating can cause electrical system damage and possible fire.

"To connect the regulator to the LP tank:
1. Make sure the LP tank is properly secured onto the grill.

5. Do not use a POL transport plug. <PIC>
6. Hold the regulator and insert the nipple into the LP tank valve. Hand-tighten the coupling nut while keeping the regulator in a straight line with the LP tank valve, so it does not cross-thread. The nipple must be centered. <PIC>
7. Turn the coupling nut clockwise and tighten to a full stop.", ["Manual19_16", "Manual19_17", "Manual19_18"]

"Leak test outdoors in a well-ventilated area, away from ignition sources, open flames or sparks. Do not smoke, and do not use an open flame to check for leaks. Use a clean paintbrush with a 50/50 mild soap and water solution and brush it onto the indicated areas.

For valves, hose and regulator:
1. Turn all grill control knobs to OFF.
2. Make sure the regulator is tightly connected to the LP tank.
3. Completely open the LP tank valve by turning the OPD hand wheel counterclockwise.
4. If you hear a rushing sound, turn gas off immediately; this indicates a major leak at the connection. Correct it before proceeding by calling Sears for replacement parts at 1-800-4-MY-HOME.

If a leak is detected at any time, STOP and call the fire department. If you cannot stop a gas leak, immediately close the LP tank valve and call your LP gas supplier or fire department.", []

Start the engine, look in all directions, make sure no boats, obstructions, or swimmers are around, then accelerate to planing speed. <PIC>", ["Manual20_90", "Manual20_91", "Manual20_92"]

"If it is difficult to balance the watercraft at a standstill, have the passenger steady the watercraft while the operator boards. The operator should pull himself up onto the platform into a seating position, then balance the watercraft. Do not operate if total weight exceeds 160 kg (353 lb), including cargo. <PIC>", ["Manual20_90"]
"Maximum load: 160 kg (353 lb), including the total weight of cargo, operator, and passenger.", []

"The manual shows two base station versions: Base station (XL490) <PIC> and Base station (XL495) <PIC>. The type plate is located on the bottom of the base station. The bottom also has the DC input jack for the power adapter and the telephone socket for the line cord.", ["Manual22_2", "Manual22_3"]

"Connect the power adapter to the DC input jack on the bottom of the base station and to the wall power socket. Then connect the line cord to the telephone socket on the bottom of the base station and to the wall telephone socket. <PIC>", ["Manual22_22"]
"The handset batteries are pre-installed. Before charging, pull the battery tape off from the battery door. <PIC>", ["Manual22_23"]

"Check the battery icon on the handset display. <PIC> When the handset is off the base station, the bars show the battery level: full, medium, or low. When on the base station/charger, the bars flash until charging is complete. An empty flashing battery icon means the battery is low and needs recharging. <PIC>", ["Manual22_28", "Manual22_29"]
"If your handset is in searching status: make sure the base station has power supply, register the handset to the base station, and move the handset closer to the base station.", []

"You can identify the status from the LED behavior as follows:

Handset LED: On = audio boost is on; Off = in a call or standby mode; Flashing = new message, new voicemail, missed call, or phone muted. For charging status: On = handset is on the base/charging cradle in standby mode or audio boost is on during a call; Off = handset is off the base/charging cradle; Flashing = phone muted. <PIC>

Base station LED: Steady on = no new message and memory not full, handset switched on, or paging mode; Flashing = new message, incoming call, recording, playback, or remote access; Fast flashing = memory full or registration mode. <PIC>", ["Manual22_40", "Manual22_46"]

"On the base station, the LED indicator shows:
- Steady on: no new message and memory is not full; the handset is switched on; paging mode.
- Flashing: new message and memory is not full; incoming call; recording an incoming message/announcement; message playback; remote access/listening to messages from the handset.
- Fast flashing: no new message and memory is full; registration mode. <PIC>", ["Manual22_46"]

"Lower the roll bar only when absolutely necessary. Remove the hairpin cotters and the 2 pins, then lower the roll bar to one of the down positions. Do not wear the seat belt when the roll bar is down; drive slowly and raise it again as soon as clearance permits. <PIC>", ["Manual23_33"]

"For machines with the suspension system only: set the rear-shock assemblies to the position that feels most comfortable. The slots have detent positions for reference, but the assemblies can be positioned anywhere in the slot, not only at the detents. Figure 13 shows the softest, firmest, and detent positions. <PIC> Adjust both rear-shock assemblies as shown, and ensure the left and right assemblies are always set to the same positions. <PIC>", ["Manual23_37", "Manual23_38"]

"For machines with an electric deck lift: push up on the deck-lift switch to raise the deck; push down to lower it. <PIC> Then select the hole in the height-of-cut bracket for the desired cutting height and insert the height-of-cut pin. <PIC>", ["Manual23_55", "Manual23_56"]

"Use extreme caution when loading the machine onto a trailer or truck. Do not use dual ramps; use one ramp wide enough for the machine with a slope less than 15°. The ramp length should be at least 4 times the height of the trailer or truck bed from the ground. Back the machine up the ramp when loading, and drive it forward down the ramp when unloading. Avoid sudden acceleration or deceleration on the ramp.", []
"The provided manual excerpts do not include instructions for unloading the lawn mower.", []

"Change the engine oil every 100 hours, or more often in dirty/dusty conditions. Start the engine and let it run for 5 minutes. Disengage the blade-control switch (PTO), engage the parking brake, shut off the engine, remove the key, and wait for all moving parts to stop. Drain the oil from the engine—Kawasaki: <PIC>; Kohler: <PIC>. Dispose of used oil at a recycling center. Slowly pour about 80% of the specified oil into the filler tube, then add oil until it reaches the Full mark—Kawasaki: <PIC>; Kohler: <PIC>. Start the engine, drive to a flat area, and check the oil level again.", ["Manual23_75", "Manual23_86", "Manual23_76", "Manual23_87"]

"To remove the filters: park the machine on a level surface, disengage the blade-control switch (PTO), and engage the parking brake. Shut off the engine, remove the key, and wait for all moving parts to stop. Release the latches on the air cleaner and pull the cover off the air-cleaner body. <PIC> Then gently slide the primary filter out; avoid knocking it against the side of the body. <PIC>", ["Manual23_72", "Manual23_82"]

"To replace the mower belt: 1. Park the machine on a level surface, disengage the blade-control switch (PTO), and engage the parking brake. 2. Shut off the engine, remove the key, and wait for all moving parts to stop. 3. Lower the mower to the 76 mm (3 inch) height of cut. 4. Use a 3/8-inch ratchet in the square hole in the idler arm to remove tension on the idler spring. 5. Remove the belt from the mower-deck pulleys and the clutch pulley. 6. Remove the belt guide on the spring-loaded idler arm. 7. Remove the existing belt. 8. Install the new belt around the mower pulleys and the clutch pulley under the engine. 9. Install the belt guide on the idler arm. <PIC>", ["Manual23_100"]

"Use the Control Set-Up pad on the control panel. It lets you change the default values for beep sound, clock display, display scroll speed, and defrost weight units (LBS/KG). Available choices include sound ON/OFF, clock ON/OFF, slow/normal/fast scroll speed, and lbs./kg. <PIC><PIC>", ["Manual24_5", "Manual24_9"]

"To set the Light Timer: touch Light Timer (press once for AM, twice for PM), enter the time you want the light to turn on, touch Light Timer again (press once for AM, twice for PM), enter the time you want the light to turn off, then touch Start. The light will come on at the low setting at the same time every day and turn off at the set time until reset. <PIC>", ["Manual24_11"]
"To program a Favorite Recipe (example: 2 minutes): touch Favorite Recipe, enter the cook time with the number keypad [2], [0], [0], then touch Start. <PIC>", ["Manual24_16"]
"Touch the Reheat pad to reheat casseroles, dinner plates, and soup or sauce. The oven’s sensor will automatically determine the cooking time based on the humidity from the food.", []

"Use Auto Defrost for meat, poultry, or fish by weight. Touch Auto Defrost, choose the food category: Meat [1], Poultry [2], Fish [3] <PIC>. Enter the net food weight in pounds and tenths, then touch Start <PIC>. During the defrost cycle, the oven beeps; open the door and turn, separate, or rearrange the food. Use Auto Defrost only for raw food; available weight is 0.1–6.0 lb.", ["Manual24_32", "Manual24_33"]

"Remove and clean the grease filter often, at least once a month. Slide the filter to the side, pull it downward, then push it to the other side so it drops out. <PIC> Soak/wash it in hot water with mild detergent, rinse well, and shake to dry. Do not use ammonia or place it in a dishwasher; the aluminum filter will darken. <PIC> Reinstall by sliding it into the side slot, then push up and toward the oven center to lock. <PIC> Do not operate the oven hood without the filter in place.", ["Manual24_47", "Manual24_48", "Manual24_49"]

"If the oven is vented inside, replace the charcoal filter every 6–12 months; it cannot be cleaned. 1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply. 2. Remove the two vent grill mounting screws (2 middle screws). <PIC> 3. Tip the grill forward, then lift it out, and remove the old filter. <PIC> 4. Slide a new charcoal filter into place; it should rest at the angle shown. <PIC> 5. Slide the bottom of the grill into place, push the top until it snaps into place, replace the screws, turn power back on, and set the clock.", ["Manual24_50", "Manual24_51", "Manual24_52"]

"To replace the oven light: 1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply. 2. Remove the vent cover mounting screws (2 middle screws), tip the cover forward, then lift it out. <PIC> 3. Remove the bulb holder. <PIC> 4. Lift up the bulb holder. <PIC> 5. Replace the bulb with a 30 or 40 watt appliance bulb. 6. Replace the bulb holder. 7. Slide the bottom of the vent cover into place, push the top until it snaps into place, and replace the mounting screws. 8. Turn the power back on or plug in the oven. Wear gloves when replacing the light bulb.", ["Manual24_54", "Manual24_55", "Manual24_56"]

"The motherboard has three PCI Express 3.0 x16 slots. For best performance with a single VGA/PCIe card, use the PCIe 3.0 x16_1 gray slot. Operating modes: single card: x16_1 runs at x16; dual cards: x16_1 and x16_2 run at x8/x8; triple cards: x16_1, x16_2, x16_3 run at x8/x8/x4. <PIC> In BIOS, PCIEx16_1/PCIEx16_2 Link Speed can be set to [Auto], [Gen1], [Gen2], or [Gen3].", ["Manual25_31"]

"For the CPU Over Voltage jumper (CPU_OV), insert the jumper on pins 2-3 to enable/gain more CPU voltage. Insert it on pins 1-2 to return to the default CPU voltage setting (disabled/default). <PIC> Do not place jumper caps on fan connectors; they are not jumpers.", ["Manual25_34"]

"The rear panel connector layout is shown here <PIC>. The manual identifies: 1. PS/2 Mouse/Keyboard combo port for a PS/2 mouse or keyboard; 2. DisplayPort for DisplayPort-compatible devices; 3. VGA port for a VGA monitor or other VGA-compatible devices.", ["Manual25_35"]

"You can turn off or change the onboard LEDs from the BIOS or the LED Control app in Ai Suite 3. In BIOS, go to Advanced > Onboard Devices Configuration, then select Model Name LED Lighting or SupremeFX LED Lighting. Model name LED options are Disabled, Still Mode, and Breathing Mode <PIC>. SupremeFX LED modes include Breathing, Flowing, and Still <PIC>.", ["Manual25_56", "Manual25_58"]

"You can update the BIOS using EZ Flash 3 or BIOS Updater.

EZ Flash 3: Enter BIOS Advanced Mode, go to Tool > EZ Flash 3 Utility, then choose either by USB or by Internet. <PIC> For USB, insert the USB flash disk with the latest BIOS file, select the USB drive, choose the BIOS file, and press Enter to start the update. For Internet, select the connection method and follow the onscreen instructions. Reboot when finished.

BIOS Updater in FreeDOS: prepare the support DVD and a FAT32/16 USB flash drive with the latest BIOS file and BIOS Updater. At the FreeDOS prompt, type bupdater /pc /g and press Enter. Select drive D:, choose the BIOS file, press Enter, then select Yes to confirm. <PIC>", ["Manual25_61", "Manual25_63"]

"To create RAID on the motherboard: connect your HDDs to the Intel SATA 6.0 Gb/s connectors, then set SATA Mode in BIOS to [RAID]. <PIC> In BIOS, press <F11> or click EZ Tuning Wizard, click RAID and Yes to enable RAID. Make sure the HDDs have no existing RAID volumes. When available HDDs are shown, click Next. <PIC> Select Easy Backup or Super Speed; for Super Speed, choose RAID0 or RAID5, then click Next. <PIC> Click Yes to continue the RAID setup. When finished, click Yes to exit, then OK to reset the system. Supported RAID configurations include RAID 0, 1, 5, and 10.", ["Manual25_48", "Manual25_72", "Manual25_75"]

"Method 1: Use SATA ODD & USB devices. Requirements: support DVD, OS 7 installation source, SATA ODD, and a USB device (ODD or storage; USB storage needs 8 GB or more and is recommended to be formatted). Steps: 1. Insert the OS 7 installation DVD into a USB ODD, or copy all files from the OS 7 DVD to a USB storage device on a working system. 2. Connect the USB ODD or USB storage device to the 100 series platform. 3. Insert the support DVD into a SATA ODD on the platform. 4. Power on and press F8 during POST to enter the boot screen. 5. Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the OS 7 installation.", []
"Place nine screws into the holes indicated by circles to secure the motherboard to the chassis. Do not over tighten the screws, as this can damage the motherboard. <PIC>", ["Manual25_6"]

"Before installing the CPU, unplug all power cables. Use only a CPU designed for the LGA1151 socket; do not install LGA1150, LGA1155, or LGA1156 CPUs. Ensure the CPU is firmly clicked into the CPU Installation Tool before placing it onto the motherboard CPU socket. Use the CPU Installation Tool only for CPU installation, do not bend or damage it, and always hold both sides when handling it. <PIC>", ["Manual25_9"]

"The motherboard has four DDR4 DIMM sockets. Use only DDR4 modules; do not install DDR, DDR2, or DDR3 modules. DIMM voltage below 1.65 V is recommended. To view memory details, use BIOS SPD Information, which displays the SPD information for the DIMM installed in the selected slot: DIMM_A1, DIMM_B1, DIMM_A2, or DIMM_B2. <PIC>", ["Manual25_18"]

"The Serial port connector (10-1 pin COM) is for a serial (COM) port. Connect the serial port module cable to this connector, then install the module to a slot opening at the back of the system chassis. The COM module is purchased separately. <PIC>", ["Manual25_39"]

"The TPM connector (14-1 pin TPM) supports a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) system. It securely stores keys, digital certificates, passwords, and data. It also helps enhance network security, protect digital identities, and ensure platform integrity. <PIC>", ["Manual25_40"]

"The 2-pin T_SENSOR connector is for a thermistor cable, which lets you monitor the temperature of the motherboard’s critical components and connected devices. The thermistor cable is purchased separately; the connector pins are SENSOR IN and GND. <PIC> In the BIOS Monitor menu, T_Sensor Temperature can be displayed, or set to [Ignore] if you do not want to display it. <PIC>", ["Manual25_43", "Manual25_83"]

"To set Quick Release, press the quick release button down until it clicks and locks into the Vent position <PIC>. Steam will eject from the top of the steam release valve; when pressure is fully released, the float valve drops into the lid <PIC>.", ["multi-use_pressure_cooker_and_air_fryer_01", "multi-use_pressure_cooker_and_air_fryer_02"]

"Use the pressure cooking lid for Pressure Cook, Sauté, Slow Cook, Steam, and Sous Vide functions. Before use, install the sealing ring in the lid—only one sealing ring should be installed at a time. Do not cover or block the steam release valve. <PIC>", ["multi-use_pressure_cooker_and_air_fryer_03"]

"To install/set the float valve: drop the narrow end of the float valve into the float valve hole on the top of the lid <PIC>. Place one finger on the flat top of the float valve, turn the lid over, then firmly attach the silicone cap to the bottom of the float valve <PIC>. Do not operate the cooker without the float valve and silicone cap properly installed.", ["Manual30_36", "Manual30_37"]

"The anti-block shield prevents food particles from coming up through the steam release pipe and helps with pressure regulation. It is integral to product safety and is necessary for pressure cooking. To install it, place the anti-block shield over the prongs and press down until it snaps into position. Do not operate the pressure cooker without the anti-block shield installed. <PIC>", ["Manual30_34"]

"Use the quick release button to control the steam release valve: flick it to the Seal position to seal, or press it to the Vent position to release pressure. Do not turn the quick release button more than 45°, and let it spring back. <PIC>", ["Manual30_14"]

"To install the anti-block shield, place it over the prongs and press down until it snaps into position. Do not operate the pressure cooker without the anti-block shield installed. <PIC>", ["Manual30_34"]

"To install, drop the narrow end of the float valve into the float valve hole on the top of the lid. <PIC> Place one finger on the flat top of the float valve, then turn the lid over and firmly attach the silicone cap to the bottom of the float valve. <PIC> Do not operate the pressure cooker unless the float valve and silicone cap are properly installed in the pressure cooking lid.", ["Manual30_36", "Manual30_37"]

"Align the grooves on the condensation collector over the tabs on the back of the cooker base, then slide the condensation collector into place. It should be installed before cooking, then emptied and rinsed after each use. <PIC>", ["Manual30_38"]

"To install the sealing ring, place it over the sealing ring rack and press it into place. Press down firmly to prevent puckering. When properly installed, it should sit snugly behind the sealing ring rack and should not fall out when the lid is turned over. <PIC>", ["Manual30_30"]

"To remove the silicone sealing ring, grip the edge of the silicone and pull the sealing ring out from behind the circular stainless-steel sealing ring rack. It is easiest to remove when wet and soapy. After removal, inspect the steel rack to make sure it is secured, centered, and even all the way around the lid.", []

"The sealing ring creates an air-tight seal between the pressure cooking lid and the inner pot when the lid is closed. It must be installed before using the cooker, and only one sealing ring should be installed in the lid at a time. Use only authorized Multi-use pressure cooker and air fryer sealing rings; do not use a stretched or damaged ring. Before cooking, always check it for cuts, deformation, and correct installation. Sealing rings stretch over time and should be replaced every 12–18 months, or sooner if stretched, deformed, or damaged. Silicone can absorb strong aromas and flavors, so keeping extra sealing rings can help limit flavor transfer between dishes. <PIC>", ["Manual30_16"]

"The steam release valve sits loosely on the steam release pipe. When pressure is released, steam ejects from the top, so keep exposed skin away. It is essential for product safety and pressure cooking, and must not be covered or blocked. <PIC> The quick release button controls whether pressure is released: flick to seal, press to vent. <PIC> Before using the pressure-cooking lid, check the steam release valve, steam release pipe, anti-block shield, and float valve for clogging. The valve must be installed before use; remove it by pulling it up and off the steam release pipe, and install it by placing it on the pipe and pressing down firmly. <PIC>", ["Manual30_15", "Manual30_14", "Manual30_32"]

"The quick release button controls the steam release valve, which determines whether pressure is released. It has Seal and Vent positions: flick to seal, press to vent. For Quick Release, press the button down until it clicks and locks into Vent; this stops cooking quickly and helps prevent overcooking, especially for quick-cooking vegetables and delicate seafood. When pressed, steam jets from the top of the steam release valve—this is normal. When pressure is fully released, the float valve drops into the lid. <PIC> <PIC> <PIC>", ["Manual30_14", "multi-use_pressure_cooker_and_air_fryer_01", "multi-use_pressure_cooker_and_air_fryer_02"]

"Natural Release (NR/NPR) is a venting method used after pressure cooking before opening the lid. Cooking stops gradually; as the cooker’s temperature drops, it depressurizes naturally over time. To use NR, leave the quick release button in the Seal position (popped up) after cooking completes, and turn Keep Warm off. The meal continues to cook after the Smart Program ends; depressurization time varies and may take up to 40 minutes. When pressure is fully released, the float valve drops into the lid. Use NR for high-starch foods such as soups, stews, chilis, pasta, oatmeal and congee, or foods that expand such as beans and grains. <PIC>", ["Manual30_9"]

"The vacuum’s robot anatomy includes: top components—iAdapt Localization Camera, Handle, and Bin Release Button <PIC>; buttons and indicators—CLEAN, DOCK, SPOT, Wi‑Fi Indicator, Troubleshooting Indicator, Battery Indicator, Full Bin Indicator, and Dirt Detect Indicator <PIC>; bottom components—Extractor Caps, Debris Extractors, Dust Bin, Extractor Frame, Extractor Frame Release Tabs, Side Brush, Charging Contacts, and Floor Tracking Sensor <PIC>.", ["Manual32_1", "Manual32_2", "Manual32_3"]

"The provided manual excerpt only states that the Dual Mode Virtual Wall Barrier can be set to one of two modes to fit your home’s cleaning needs, but it does not specify the names of those two modes.", []
"Press the bin release button to remove the bin <PIC>. Then open the bin door and empty the bin <PIC>. After each use, empty the bin and clean the filter.", ["Manual32_8", "Manual32_9"]

"To clean the filter: remove the filter by grasping the yellow tab <PIC>. Shake off debris by tapping the filter against your trash container <PIC>. Reinsert the filter with the yellow tab facing up; the filter door will not close unless the filter is reinserted.", ["Manual32_10", "Manual32_11"]

"To clean the full bin sensors: 1. Remove and empty the bin. <PIC> 2. Wipe the sensors with a clean, dry cloth. <PIC> 3. Wipe the inner and outer sensor ports on the bin with a clean, dry cloth. <PIC>", ["Manual32_12", "Manual32_13", "Manual32_14"]

"To clean the extractors: 1. Pinch the yellow extractor frame release tabs, lift the extractor frame, and remove any obstructions. <PIC> 2. Remove the extractors and yellow extractor caps; clear hair or debris from under the caps and around the metal axles, then reinstall the caps. <PIC> 3. Remove hair and debris from the square and hexagonal plastic pegs on the other side of the extractors. <PIC> 4. Clear the vacuum path. <PIC> 5. Reinstall the extractors, matching the color and shape of the extractor pegs with the icons on the cleaning head module.", ["Manual32_19", "Manual32_20", "Manual32_21", "Manual32_22"]

"Wipe the sensor with a clean, dry cloth. Do not spray cleaning solution directly onto the sensors or sensor openings. <PIC> Then wipe the charging contacts on the vacuum and the Home Base with a clean, dry cloth. <PIC>", ["Manual32_17", "Manual32_18"]

"Place the Home Base in an open, uncluttered area: leave at least 1.5 ft on each side, at least 4 ft in front, at least 4 ft away from stairs, and at least 8 ft from virtual wall barriers. Keep it plugged in and in an area with consistent coverage so the vacuum can receive app information.", []

"To clean the front caster wheel: 1. Pull firmly on the front wheel to remove it. <PIC> 2. Remove any debris from inside the wheel cavity. 3. Spin the wheel by hand. If rotation is restricted, remove the wheel from its housing, push firmly to remove the axle, and clear any debris or hair wrapped around it. 4. Reinstall all parts when finished, making sure the wheel clicks back into place.", ["Manual32_15"]
"To clean the side brush: use a coin or small screwdriver to remove the screw <PIC>, then remove the brush, clean the brush and the brush post, and reinstall the brush.", ["Manual32_16"]

"The dual-mode virtual wall barrier keeps the vacuum in areas you want cleaned and out of areas you don’t. It has two modes: Halo Mode creates an invisible protective zone the vacuum will not enter, and Virtual Wall Mode creates an invisible cone-shaped barrier to block openings up to 10 ft.", []

"If the vacuum indicates a problem, it will make a two-tone distress sound followed by a spoken message, and the troubleshooting indicator will blink. Check the app or online for more detailed support and videos. For some errors, rebooting may resolve the problem: press and hold CLEAN for 10 seconds until all indicators illuminate, then release. A tone confirms a successful reboot. If you use scheduling, open the app after rebooting to confirm the schedule remains intact.", []

"T-rail mounting instructions: Use the included hardware to mount the camera on a drop-ceiling T-rail; it supports most 9/16\", 15/16\", or 1 1/2\" T-rails. 1) Using the dashed lines on the mount plate template as a guide, set the proper spacing of the clips. <PIC> 2) Tighten the set screws on the T-rail clips with a 5/64\" (2 mm) hex key. <PIC> 3) Attach the mount plate to the T-rail clips using the mount plate holes marked “G”. <PIC> 4) Attach the T-rail clips to the T-rail by rotating them and snapping them into place as shown; the black foam pads should be slightly compressed after installation. <PIC> Use standard 6-32 x 4 mm T-rail screws; for recessed T-rail modifications, use rubber spacers and 6-32 x 7 mm screws as shown. <PIC>", ["Manual33_11", "Manual33_12", "Manual33_13", "Manual33_10", "Manual33_14"]

"To power the camera, set the power switch to <ON>; the camera can operate only after the switch is turned on. Set it to <OFF> to turn the camera off. If it turns off automatically after being idle, press the shutter button to turn it on again. <PIC>", ["Manual10_29"]

"Squeeze the brake lever toward the handlebar to stop the machine; the brake light will illuminate when the brake is operated. <PIC> When parking or starting the engine, apply the parking brake: squeeze the brake lever, push down the parking brake button while releasing the brake lever. To release the parking brake, simply squeeze the brake lever. Always set the parking brake before starting the engine, and never run the machine with the parking brake applied. <PIC>", ["Manual34_39", "Manual34_40"]

"Before using the snowmobile: read the Owner’s Manual, warning/caution labels, and safety/riding sections; become familiar with all controls; perform the manual’s pre-operation checks before riding; wear an approved helmet, eye/face protection, snowmobile suit, boots, and gloves/mittens; check the drive select lever position before moving; ensure the fuel tank cap is securely closed after refueling; and do not operate the engine without the drive belt or drive guard.", []

"To start the snowmobile engine (manual starting model): 1. Set the parking brake. 2. Turn the main switch to the “ON” position. 3. Pull slowly on the recoil starter until it is engaged, then pull it briskly. <PIC> 4. After the engine starts, put the starter lever/choke in the “Half-open” position. 5. Warm up the engine until it does not run roughly or begin to stall when the starter lever is returned to the “Close” position.", ["Manual34_116"]
"A V-belt holder is the provided holder used to keep a spare V-belt for emergency use.", []

"Before adjusting, be sure the engine idle speed is adjusted first. 1. Loosen the adjuster lock nut. 2. Turn the adjuster in or out until the proper throttle lever free play is achieved: BR250T/ET410TR/VK540E: 1.0–2.0 mm (0.04–0.08 in); CS340E: 0.5–1.0 mm (0.02–0.04 in). <PIC> 3. Tighten the locknut.", ["Manual34_148"]

"Use the steering controls with both hands on the handlebars, keeping your feet on the running boards. Avoid high speeds until you are familiar with the snowmobile and its controls. When turning, avoid abrupt throttle changes, excessive braking, incorrect body movement, or too much speed. If the snowmobile begins to tip while turning, lean more into the turn; if needed, gradually release the throttle and/or steer to the outside of the turn. <PIC> On a slope, if it slips sideways, steer in the direction of the slide if clear, then gradually steer where you want to go; if it starts to tip, steer down the hill. <PIC>", ["Manual34_127", "Manual34_129"]

"To turn correctly: keep speed low until you are thoroughly familiar with the snowmobile; avoid abrupt throttle changes, excessive braking, incorrect body movements, and entering a turn too fast. If the snowmobile begins to tip while turning, lean more into the turn to regain balance. If needed, gradually ease off the throttle and/or steer toward the outside of the turn. <PIC>", ["Manual34_127"]

"For riding uphill, first practice on gentle slopes and attempt more difficult climbs only after developing your skill. As you approach a hill, accelerate before starting the climb, then reduce the throttle opening to prevent track slippage. If the snowmobile slows on a hill, do not spin the track; stop the engine, set the parking brake, pull the rear around so it points downhill, stay off the down-hill side, then restart, release the brake, and descend. <PIC>", ["Manual34_127"]

"When riding downhill, keep speed to a minimum. Apply just enough throttle to keep the clutch engaged so engine compression helps slow the machine and prevents it from rolling freely downhill. Apply the brake frequently with light pressure. <PIC> Use extra caution: excessive braking can lock the track and cause loss of control.", ["Manual34_128"]

"When crossing a slope (side hill), position your weight toward the uphill side by leaning your body uphill. A recommended position is to kneel with the downhill knee on the seat and place the uphill foot on the running board so you can shift weight as needed. If the snowmobile slips sideways, steer in the direction of the slide if there are no obstacles; once balanced, gradually steer back toward your intended direction. If it starts to tip, steer down the hill to regain balance. If you cannot maintain balance and it is going to tip over, dismount immediately on the uphill side. Side hills are not recommended for beginners. <PIC>", ["Manual34_129"]

"To inspect the spark plug: 1. Periodically remove the spark plug. 2. Check the coloration on the white porcelain insulator around the center electrode; ideal color is medium to light tan. 3. If the center electrode porcelain is very white, do not diagnose it yourself—take the machine to your dealer. 4. Before installing, use a spark plug with the proper reach <PIC>. 5. Measure the electrode gap with a wire thickness gauge and adjust to specification <PIC>. 6.
